# Subsystem: pipeline (element-wise pipeline engine, op plumbing, SIMD scalar layer)

## Purpose

Fuses a tree of element-wise ops into one strided n-d loop. `Op1` / `Op2` / `MapMultiple` / `Clamp`
implement `read_data` as `check_out_buf` + `context.read_cached(id, ..)` around
`self.read_as_elementwise_pipeline::<Out>(index, ctx)?.to_buf(index, ctx, out)` (op1.rs:58-69,
op2.rs:113-124, map.rs:301-312). Building the pipeline reads every *leaf* region up front: the
default leaf is `read_data_pull` wrapped in `OperandTyped` (storage/core_trait.rs:113-125); `Scalar`
is a `Constant` node with no operand (storage/scalar.rs:125-160). `to_buf`
(ops/elementwise/pipeline.rs:63-123) materializes the output, walks all operands (output = operand
0) with `NdIterUnordered`, optionally stages operands into scratch, and calls `inner_loop`, which pulls
`[T; LANES]` through `read_bulk` and stores it. `scalar/simd.rs` + `scalar/traits_util.rs` generate the
per-type scalar fn and SIMD `*_bulk` fn that kernels call inside `read_bulk`. All `pipeline.rs` refs
below are `jix/src/ops/elementwise/pipeline.rs` (moved from `storage/elementwise_pipeline.rs` in #97/#98).

## Contracts

Node contract - `ElementwisePipelineImpl<T>` (pipeline.rs:27-61, pub(crate)); the pub
`ElementwisePipeline` (:24-25) has it as a private bound, so nobody outside the crate can implement or
call it:
- `N_OPERANDS` (:29): the exact number of `&Operand`s `operands()` yields, or `None`. `to_buf` picks
  `to_buf_impl::<1 + n>` for 1+n <= 16 at compile time (:82-115), else `to_buf_impl_dyn`.
  `to_buf_impl` fills `[&Operand; N]` with `operand_iter.next().unwrap()` (:139): an overcount panics;
  an undercount is only `debug_assert!`ed (:140) - the extra operands never get a cursor, keep
  `current_ptr == null` (:775) and a release build reads `null + offset`. Combinators:
  `n_operands_sum` / `n_operands_mul` (:955-986); `Constant` = Some(0); Vec / slice sequences = None
  (util/arr_sequence.rs:420, :545); `[Array; N]` = mul (:222, :319); tuples = sum (:681).
- `MAX_ITEMSIZE` (:33): max size of the leaves, every intermediate value and the output. Only sizes
  the contiguous lane count (`inner_loop_per_level` :684-702, see below). Too small -> bigger stack
  arrays, never memory unsafety; 0 -> const-eval division by zero (compile error).
- `operands()` (:36): every leaf `read_bulk` touches must be yielded (only yielded operands get a
  cursor). Order only affects dim sorting / staging heuristics / pull layout; output is index 0.
  Select yields (x, y, condition) although it reads condition first (ops/elementwise/select.rs:369-375).
- `read_bulk::<N, CONTIGUOUS, S>(offset, status, simd)` (:56-61, unsafe): reads elements
  `offset..offset+N` of the current run from every child at the same `offset`; nothing is advanced
  (:40-42). The `Operand` docs saying the cursor "advances" (:735, :740) are stale. Safety (:51-55):
  each operand's `current_ptr` aligned for its dtype when `REQUIRE_ALIGNED`, and `offset..offset+N`
  at `inner_stride` in bounds of the buffer the cursor points at (original data OR a staging buffer).
  `CONTIGUOUS` promises `inner_stride == itemsize` for EVERY operand; `OperandTyped` (:836-863) then
  reads `[T; N]` at `base + offset*size_of::<T>()` and only `debug_assert`s the stride (:849). Caller:
  `inner_loop_impl` (:590-649) with `len` = chunk length set by the drivers; nodes forward the same
  `offset`/`status` (op1.rs:111-119, op2.rs:174-180, map.rs:356-366, select.rs:384-390, min_max.rs:335-342).
- Kernels never panic or return early on arithmetic errors: write a fallback value and OR a flag into
  `status` (:45-49). Since #95 the only flags are integer `DivideByZero` / `NegativePower`
  (error.rs:314-327); floats report nothing. SIMD bodies and scalar fns must agree bit-for-bit and on
  status: the same element goes through the SIMD body or the scalar fn depending on its position (tail
  `N=1` at :636-647; `N % lanes != 0` falls back to the scalar fn in scalar/simd.rs:184, :226, :338)
  and on strides / CPU (contiguous runs use runtime `SimdLevel::new()`, strided use compile-time
  `dispatch_baseline!`, :662-666; `map_masks_to_bools` uses SIMD only on AVX2, simd.rs:338).
- `Op1/Op2/MapMultiple/Clamp` nodes run `check_dtype(T, Output)` when the pipeline is built, then
  `transmute_copy` `[K::Output; N] -> [T; N]` behind a const size assert (op1.rs:80, :117-119;
  op2.rs:135, :178-180; map.rs:323, :362-364; min_max.rs:286, :362-364). Soundness rests on the
  `unsafe trait Dtyped` contract (dtype.rs:1153-1171): equal `Dtype` => same size, alignment, layout,
  every bit pattern valid. `Select` does no transmute; its children check `T` themselves.

Driver (`to_buf_type_erased` :193-311, `_dyn` :313-442 - byte-for-byte identical apart from array vs
Vec; verified by diff at 0371e75):
- Region shape is `index.size()` (:201-209). `Index` guarantees ndim <= 8, equal lengths, no zero size,
  no `start+size` overflow (storage/index.rs:10-14, :52-61). The old empty-region early return is gone
  (#103): `debug_assert!(!shape.contains(&0))` (:211, :335). A dim where every operand INCLUDING the
  output has stride 0 is collapsed to length 1 (:203-207). Region-in-shape is checked earlier by
  `check_out_buf` -> `check_get_range` (storage/buf.rs:351-363) in the op's `read_data`; on 32-bit
  `check_region_size` bounds `prod(size) * out_itemsize <= isize::MAX` (error.rs:297-312); on 64-bit
  `check_shape_overflow` at construction bounds the product to u64 (op1.rs:35, op2.rs:52, map.rs:245).
- `NdIterUnordered::new(shape, byte strides, (itemsize, alignment) per operand)` (:220) sorts /
  drops len-1 dims / coalesces; asserts every stride slice has `shape.len()` entries
  (util/nd_iter_unordered.rs:70-72); an all-size-1 region reports inner stride = itemsize, contiguous
  AND strides-aligned regardless of the real strides (:87-96).
- Chunks of `chunk_len_max = min(inner_len, 8192)` elements (:221, `Staging::BUFFER_SIZE` :510).
  Per chunk each cursor is set to `base + offset + pos*inner_stride` (:251-276) or to its staging buffer
  with stride = itemsize; `dst` becomes a `PtrMutNoalias` (`&mut [u8]`, noalias) over the output chunk
  span (:278-284).
- `InnerLoopFlags` (:239-243): operand contiguous iff NdIter says so OR it is staged.
  `inner_loop_impl` does `assert_unchecked(OUT_CONTIGUOUS == (dst_stride == size_of::<T>()))` (:606):
  holds because the flag and `dst_stride` come from the same inner stride (or itemsize when staged) and
  `Dtyped` itemsize == `size_of::<T>()`.
- Staging (`compute_need_staging` :465-498): (a) `REQUIRE_ALIGNED` (all targets except x86, x86_64,
  aarch64 - util/mod.rs:653-657) and operand base or any coalesced stride not a multiple of the dtype
  alignment (:478-480); (b) non-contiguous INPUTS when >= 4 inputs are contiguous and they are >= half
  (:445-460, :481); (c) inputs with inner stride 0 when `inner_len >= 64` and every other operand is
  contiguous or staged (:486-497). The output is staged only by (a); it is scattered back with
  `Staging::write_to` after each chunk (:295-306).
- `Staging::fill_from` (:528-560) skips the copy when `(src, stride)` match the last fill and
  `prev_n >= n`; stride 0 records `n = usize::MAX`. The stride-0 shortcut is correct only because the
  first fill of any `src` at stride 0 is at `pos == 0` with the full `chunk_len_max` (every later chunk
  of a stride-0 operand has the same `src`). Pool buffers start with stale bytes (util/buf_pool.rs:39-50).
- Status: per-chunk status ORed, `status.into_result()` once at the very end (:310, :441;
  error.rs:371-391): the whole region is written BEFORE the Err is returned.

Output materialization (`to_buf` :63-123, `materialize_pipeline_out_buf` :866-886,
`pick_output_layout` :888-945, `make_readonly_if_aliasing` :947-953):
- Push (`OutBufInner::Push`): the caller's `&mut StridedBuf` is used as-is (:875). The op's
  `check_out_buf` -> `check_out_buf_impl` (storage/buf.rs:383-430) has already checked ndim,
  writability, no self-overlap over the region (`disjoint_span`, so no 0-stride on a len > 1 dim) and
  span <= buffer length. Nothing checks that `out` does not overlap an INPUT (caller's job, see
  Intentional behaviors).
- Pull (`OutBufInner::Pull(slot)`): dims that no input walks (all input strides 0, len > 1) get
  output stride 0 and extent 1; the rest get a packed layout in the operands' common stride order when
  all agree and the region is > 4096 bytes, else C order (:895-944). The buffer is written into the
  slot via `write_out_buf_slot` (storage/buf.rs:505-516, asserts the slot was empty). After a
  successful run, a buffer with any 0-stride len > 1 dim is made read-only (:119-121, :949-952).
  "Real dim" here (len <= 1 or some input stride != 0) and the driver's collapse rule (some operand
  incl. output stride != 0) must agree; they do because the pull output has stride 0 exactly on the
  non-real dims.
- `Operand::new_output` (:761-768) takes `base_ptr` from `data_ptr_mut().unwrap()` (never panics:
  push outs are checked writable, pull outs are fresh `PoolBufMut`) and then reborrows `out` shared
  for its strides (Miri-motivated, :748).

Read cache interplay (#100, context.rs:148-243): only `read_data` goes through `read_cached`; a
fused child's `read_as_elementwise_pipeline` bypasses it, so an op reached twice inside one fused
pipeline is computed twice (correct, just not cached). Leaves (Compact, compact.rs:246) still read
through it, so two leaves may share one read-only `Shared` buffer. On a pull miss the pipeline's
buffer is converted with `into_shared` (storage/buf.rs:337-348) and handed back read-only; on a push
hit the cached buffer (possibly with 0 strides) is copied into `out` by `OutBuf::set` (buf.rs:490-501).

Relied on from other modules: a leaf's `read_data` pull buffer covers the region at its strides (one
stride per dim; no runtime check in the pipeline; `ArrayStorage` is sealed since #90 so all impls are
in-crate); `NdCopier::copy` / `fill_contiguous` (util/nd_copy.rs:45-57, :441-471: in-bounds spans,
no overlap - true because staging buffers are separate pool allocations); `PtrNoalias::new` /
`PtrMutNoalias::new` (util/mod.rs:679-741: span valid, no other access for the lifetime);
`ReadContext::allocate_buf` returns >= size bytes aligned to max(align, cache line)
(util/buf_pool.rs:39-50, :73-78).

Pub(crate) unsafe fns and who establishes their preconditions:
- `ElementwisePipelineImpl::read_bulk` - drivers via `inner_loop_impl`; nodes forward to children.
- `ElementwisePipelineTuple::read_bulk_as_iter` (util/arr_sequence.rs:133-152): read_bulk's contract
  plus "drop the returned iterator before the next call" - `MapMultiplePipeline::read_bulk`
  (map.rs:348-367) consumes it inside the call.
- `OperandTyped::new_input` (:812-823): "valid view of `dtype` elements, dtype == T::DTYPE". Only
  caller storage/core_trait.rs:122-124: dtype via `check_dtype`, validity from the sealed `read_data`.
- `Staging::fill_from` / `write_to` (:520-586, private): the driver passes in-bounds chunk pointers.

## Unsafe inventory

- :252-256, :383-387 `base_ptr().add(offset + pos*stride)` - in bounds because offsets come from
  NdIter over the same shape/strides. Non-local: relies on each leaf buffer covering the region.
- :261-268, :392-399 `fill_from`; :298-305, :429-436 `write_to` - chunk in bounds; staging buffer holds
  `chunk_len_max` elements (allocated :233-235 / :360-366, `Staging::new` :512-518). Local.
- :279-284, :410-415 `PtrMutNoalias::new(out cursor, span)` - `&mut [u8]` over the output chunk while
  input `StridedBuf`s (often `&[u8]`) are alive. Sound only if `out` does not overlap any input: NOT
  checked anywhere; documented as the caller's obligation (storage/buf.rs:89-97, K31 intended).
- :536 `NonNull::new(src).unwrap()` (panic only on null); :542 `fill_contiguous`; :548, :574
  `PtrNoalias/PtrMutNoalias::new` with `(n-1)*stride + itemsize` spans; :550-559, :576-585 NdCopier.
  Local, except the fill cache (:530-537) which is the non-local stride-0 invariant above.
- :606 `assert_unchecked` - driver flags + Dtyped itemsize == size_of::<T>() (non-local, holds).
- :617-647 `read_bulk` calls and `write_maybe_aligned::<REQUIRE_ALIGNED>` of `[T; LANES]` / `T` -
  alignment only `debug_assert!` (:608-610); established by staging (a) and by pool alignment.
- :836-863 `OperandTyped::read_bulk` - non-null / aligned / stride only `debug_assert` (:843-849).
  Every byte pattern of `T` is valid by the Dtyped contract (bool is not Dtyped; `bool8` is).
- :885 `StridedBuf::from_pool(buf, strides)` - packed permutation layout fits `nitems * itemsize`.
- op1.rs:119, op2.rs:180, map.rs:365, min_max.rs:342, storage/scalar.rs:136 - `transmute_copy`
  behind runtime `check_dtype` + const size assert.
- op1.rs:111-114, op2.rs:174-175, map.rs:356-359 - child `read_bulk` / `read_bulk_as_iter` forwarding.
- util/arr_sequence.rs:444-456, :569-581 Vec/slice MapMultiple scratch: `&mut *UnsafeCell` (exclusive
  by the read_bulk_as_iter contract), written through `spare_capacity_mut` then `set_len` (K124 fixed).
- `scalar/simd.rs`, `scalar/traits_util.rs`, `into_type.rs`, `maybe_compact.rs`, `dims_arg.rs` contain
  no `unsafe` (fearless_simd `from_slice` / `store_slice` are bounds-checked). `scalar/bool.rs`
  unsafe is test-only (:113-124).

## Edge-case surface

- Empty regions: unrepresentable (`Index` sizes are `NonZeroUsize`); 0-d (`index = []`): NdIter
  yields one element; pull allocates one item with strides `[]`.
- Length-1 dims: dropped by NdIter; pull output keeps them "real" with a computed stride.
- Broadcast (stride 0): inputs - degenerate-dim collapse (:203-207) or staged fill (:486-497);
  output - push rejects 0 strides on len > 1 dims (`check_out_buf_impl`), so the output inner stride
  is never 0; pull returns 0-stride dims read-only to the caller.
- Mixed itemsizes (casts, comparisons to bool8, MapMultiple tuples): strides are per-operand bytes
  with per-operand `(itemsize, alignment)`; `CONTIGUOUS` means each operand's stride == ITS itemsize;
  lanes come from the widest value (`MAX_ITEMSIZE`). Dim order is lexicographic over operands with the
  output first; pull layout follows the inputs only if they all agree (:909-922).
- Loop tails: `len % LANES` handled by `read_bulk::<1>` (:636-647); `N % vector_lanes != 0` uses the
  scalar fn inside `map_vectors*` (simd.rs:184, :226, :338).
- Lanes (:684-702): contiguous in+out and `MAX_ITEMSIZE <= S::u8s::LEN` -> `(4 on x86 | 8) *
  prev_power_of_two(LEN / MAX_ITEMSIZE)` (up to 512 for u8 on AVX-512); otherwise
  `min((128 / size_of::<T>()).next_power_of_two(), 4)` (size > 128 gives `0.next_power_of_two()` = 1).
- > 16 operands, Vec / slice sequences: `to_buf_impl_dyn` + `NdIterUnorderedDyn` (duplicated code).
- NDIM_MAX = 8: `dim_arr` / `DimArray` capacity; Index guarantees ndim <= 8.
- Unaligned buffers: unaligned loads/stores on x86/aarch64; staging elsewhere (armv7 wheels are
  shipped, CI runs only x86_64, so `REQUIRE_ALIGNED = true` paths are untested).
- 32-bit: the pipeline no longer converts u64 -> usize itself (Index sizes are usize); products are
  bounded by `check_region_size` in `check_out_buf`, which every `to_buf` caller runs first.
- Huge struct dtypes: staging buffers are `chunk_len_max * itemsize` bytes (itemsize < 65536).
- f16 / Complex: not `SimdElementExt`, so bulk fns fall back to scalar loops; `Complex<f64>` (16 B)
  gives 1 value per SSE vector.
- Arithmetic status: OR-accumulated per chunk; nested non-fused leaves (reductions, shape ops over
  ops) check their own status inside their `read_data`.

## Intentional behaviors

- Rust binary / multi-input ops require identical shapes, no implicit broadcasting (op2.rs:40-53,
  map.rs:237-244); Python does the broadcasting. `Array` op methods and operator impls `unwrap()` and
  panic with `#[track_caller]` (op1.rs:239-256, :263-275; op2.rs:306-357; map.rs:408-420).
- Pull mode collapses dims no input walks: kernels / user closures run once per distinct input
  element, the returned buffer has read-only stride-0 dims; push mode writes every element (tests
  pipeline.rs:1806-1905). Visit order is unspecified (util/nd_iter_unordered.rs:7-33).
- Arithmetic errors: fallback value + flag, never a panic; integer errors always become
  `ErrorKind::Arithmetic`, floats never error (no errstate since #95, error.rs:314-345); the output
  is fully written before the Err is returned.
- Zero-itemsize output dtypes are rejected with `UnsupportedDtype` (op1.rs:34, op2.rs:39, map.rs:235;
  tests map.rs:817-850). `MapMultiple::new` with zero arrays returns InvalidShapeOperation (map.rs:237,
  test :464); with one array the shape check is trivially true (test map.rs:761).
- `out` must not overlap memory any array in the lazy chain reads: documented as the caller's
  obligation (storage/buf.rs:89-97; jix-py/src/array.rs:485-502); K31 intended.
- No alignment is promised for `StridedBuf` or required of `out` (storage/buf.rs:22-24,
  storage/core_trait.rs:89-93). Strides are unsigned: negative strides are unsupported.
- `MaybeCompact` keeps an already-compact source untouched and ignores params (maybe_compact.rs:9-13,
  :156-160; tests :306, :333).

  before the run; on an Err from `to_buf_fn` (:117) the slot keeps a WRITABLE buffer whose 0-stride

  test): correctness now rests entirely on the `Index` invariants. Is `Index::new_unchecked` ever fed a

  (storage/mod.rs:99-174, :225-270): the same storage can appear several times in one pipeline.
  Cursors live per `Operand`; is any other per-storage state (scratch, cache entry) assumed unique?

- `REQUIRE_ALIGNED = true` paths (armv7 / wasm): staged-output scatter (:295-306), base aligned but
  coalesced strides not, `[T; LANES]` aligned stores, alignment of a staged cursor.
- `pick_output_layout` (:888-945) vs the driver collapse rule: same "real dim" definition in every

- Lane math (:684-702): `[T; 512]` per node per call for u8 on AVX-512; debug builds keep every

  f32/f64 method shadowing the trait method (else infinite recursion); f16 goes through f32 and has

  bit-for-bit at every level.
- SIMD layer: `mask8s_from_mask` lane order (simd.rs:96-138), `map_masks_to_bools` AVX2-only path
  (:325-359), `map_vectors_different_width` KT/KU chunking (:162-205), `for_each_unrolled`

### Suspicions (unverified)

- [CONFIRMED in batch7-3 as K164] util/arr_sequence.rs:220, :320 - `[Array<S>; N]` / `&[Array<S>; N]` sequences report
  `MAX_ITEMSIZE = D::MAX_ITEMSIZE`, ignoring N, while `read_bulk_as_iter` holds `[[T; M]; N]` (copied
  into the `move` iterator) with M up to 512 contiguous lanes: `map_multiple([a; 2048], f)` over u8
  may need >= 1-2 MiB of stack per call and abort a 2 MiB thread (cf. K30, which fixed the itemsize).
